propositions: Production alert-lifecycle and staleness-classification logic (~200 lines) currently embedded in untestable YAML run-blocks within reconcile-bridge-canary.yml, causing defects and preventing linting/type-checking.

Four logic families (check-heartbeat, heartbeat-alert, check-binding-drift, binding-drift-alert) need extraction to a testable Python module (scripts/canary_bridge.py) while preserving error handling dispositions and DRY_RUN guards.
CAS push loops (reconcile-bridge.yml commit-back and canary flush) remain in YAML and are out of scope; only branchy classification/alert-lifecycle logic with ${{ }} expressions migrates.

Anti-rot test must pin the canary wiring (workflow parses, steps invoke the canonical Python entry point, flush loop remains byte-identical verbatim) to prevent accidental re-introduction of untestable logic blocks.

Unit tests must cover classification matrix, each lifecycle transition, error paths (API failures, rebar write failures, fsck exit codes), GITHUB_OUTPUT emission format, and DRY_RUN=true short-circuit behavior.
Post-merge operator-attested parity run required: workflow_dispatch execution must show identical staleness classification and alert behavior as the preceding pre-migration scheduled run.
